recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — reverses_request_id column, model field, repository plumbing
recommended_phases.rationale: Everything else depends on the column existing. Add the knex migration (nullable text reverses_request_id + FK to leave_requests.id + index, with a matching down()), add reversesRequestId: string | null to LeaveRequest (CreateLeaveRequestInput follows via Omit), and thread it through PgLeaveRequestRepository: COLUMNS, LeaveRequestRow, mapRow, the create INSERT column/value list, and FIELD_COLUMNS. No new repository method is needed — the reversal row is inserted with the existing create. No service logic yet, so this phase is independently verifiable by tsc + migration run.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — LeaveService.cancel reversal branch (GP-008)
recommended_phases.rationale: The behavioural core, and it depends on Phase 1's column. In cancel(), keep the DRAFT/SUBMITTED path exactly as-is (in-place update to CANCELLED). For APPROVED, replace the in-place update with repository.create of a NEW row (same employeeId/leaveTypeCode/startDate/endDate/requestedDays/reason, status CANCELLED, cancelledBy/cancelledAt set, approverId/approvalComment/submittedAt/decidedAt null, reversesRequestId = original.id) and return that new row. The approved row is never passed to update. The balance release (usedDays -= requestedDays, read with forUpdate=true), the CANCEL audit record, and the requester notification stay inside the same single uow.withTransaction and are executed exactly once. assertCanCancel and the startDate<=today guard are untouched.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — unit tests proving immutability and single release
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on Phase 2. Extend tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts: after cancelling an APPROVED request, assert the original row still reads APPROVED with approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt unchanged, that a NEW row with status CANCELLED and reversesRequestId === original.id was created, that repository.update was never called with the original id, that usedDays was released exactly once (one balance update, correct delta), that exactly one CANCEL audit entry and one notification were written, and that all of it happened inside one withTransaction callback with the client forwarded. Also assert DRAFT/SUBMITTED cancellation still mutates in place with reversesRequestId null. The FakeLeaveRepository needs create/update call recording.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — read-model exposure + smoke proof against real Postgres
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on Phases 1–3. reversesRequestId is already serialized by GET /leaves and GET /leaves/:id once the model carries it, so this phase verifies rather than adds: confirm the read model exposes reversesRequestId (null on ordinary rows) and extend scripts/smoke.js with an authenticated stage that approves a request, cancels it, then asserts GET /leaves/:id on the original still returns APPROVED and that a second row with status CANCELLED and reversesRequestId equal to the original id is present in GET /leaves. This is the acceptance test that must pass against real Postgres.

app_notes:
## Layer boundaries
- **Presentation** — `src/modules/leave/leave.routes.ts` (Fastify handlers, `resolveActor`, `parseCreateBody`/`parseQuery`, `sendError`). No controller layer (binding decision Q1). Routes call the service directly and contain no business logic.
- **Application** — `LeaveService` (`src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts`). Sole orchestrator; owns the transaction boundary via `IUnitOfWork.withTransaction` and the GP-008 reversal decision. Depends only on interfaces.
- **Domain** — `LeaveRequest` (`leave.model.ts`), `LeaveBalance`, `LeavePolicy`, `AuditLog`, `Notification`, plus the canonical enums/DTOs/`requestedDays` in `src/shared/types/`. No I/O.
- **Infrastructure** — `PgLeaveRequestRepository`, `PgLeaveBalanceRepository`, `PgAuditLogRepository`, `PgNotificationRepository`, `PgEmployeeRepository`, `PgLeavePolicyRepository`, `PgUnitOfWork`, `src/shared/db/connection.ts`, `migrations/`. All SQL lives here (GP-001).

Dependencies flow inward only: routes → service → repository interfaces → shared. Repositories never import services; shared never imports modules.

## GP-008 mechanics (the whole feature)
`cancel(actor, requestId)` branches on the loaded request's status:
- **DRAFT / SUBMITTED** — unchanged: `repository.update(requestId, { status: CANCELLED, cancelledBy, cancelledAt })` in place. No completed approval exists, so GP-008 does not apply. DRAFT still touches no balance row; SUBMITTED still releases `pendingDays -= requestedDays`.
- **APPROVED** — the approved row is **never** passed to `update`. Instead `repository.create({ ...copied span fields, status: CANCELLED, cancelledBy, cancelledAt, approverId: null, approvalComment: null, submittedAt: null, decidedAt: null, reversesRequestId: original.id })` inserts a NEW row, and that new row is what `cancel` returns. The original keeps its status, `approverId`, `approvalComment` and `decidedAt` byte-for-byte.

Everything else in the APPROVED branch is unchanged and stays inside the **same single** `uow.withTransaction`: the balance row is read with `forUpdate = true` and `usedDays -= requestedDays` exactly once (no double-release, no skip), one CANCEL audit record is written, one cancellation notification is sent to the requester. `assertCanCancel` (owner for DRAFT/SUBMITTED; direct manager or ADMIN for APPROVED) and the `startDate <= today` ConflictError guard are untouched — the guard is what makes the full, un-prorated release correct.

## Schema / repository
New knex migration adds nullable `reverses_request_id` (text, FK → `leave_requests.id`) plus an index on it; `down()` drops index then column. `LeaveRequest` gains `reversesRequestId: string | null`; `CreateLeaveRequestInput` follows via `Omit<LeaveRequest,'id'>`, so `create()` must now supply `reversesRequestId: null` for ordinary creates. `PgLeaveRequestRepository` threads the column through `COLUMNS`, `LeaveRequestRow`, `mapRow`, the INSERT list and `FIELD_COLUMNS`. **No new repository method** — the reversal row uses the existing `create`. `reversesRequestId` is deliberately **not** added to `UpdateLeaveRequestDto`/`FIELD_COLUMNS`: the link is set at insert and is immutable thereafter, which is what keeps the approved row untouchable.

## Wire contract
`GET /leaves` and `GET /leaves/:id` serialize the model, so `reversesRequestId` appears automatically (`null` on ordinary rows, the original's id on a reversal row). A client distinguishes the two rows by `status` (APPROVED vs CANCELLED) and by `reversesRequestId`. Role scoping is unaffected: the reversal row carries the same `employeeId`, so it is visible to exactly the same audience as the original.

## Dependency map verification
Edges are acyclic and all point inward: `leave → {balance, audit, notification, employee, policy, validation, shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db, shared-date}`; `balance → {policy, employee, shared-*}`; `policy → shared-*`; `employee/audit/notification/validation → shared-*`; `shared-date → {shared-errors, shared-types}`; `migrations → shared-db`. No module depends back on `leave`; no shared module depends on a module. `leave-type` is reached only through `policy` (via `createPolicyService()`), so no new edge is introduced.

## Shared-type placement
No new shared type is created. `reversesRequestId` is a field of the leave-owned `LeaveRequest` entity (owned lifecycle/state rules), so it stays in `src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts` — it is not a methodless cross-module value type and must not be hoisted into `src/shared/types/`. `LeaveStatus.CANCELLED` and `AuditAction.CANCEL` already exist in `src/shared/types/` and are reused, not redeclared.

open_questions.question: For the APPROVED reversal, which id does the CANCEL audit record's entityId carry — the original approved request id or the newly inserted CANCELLED row's id?
open_questions.impact: The audit trail is the only record of who reversed what. Pointing entityId at the original keeps the reversal discoverable from the approved request's history but makes the new row's own creation unaudited; pointing it at the new row leaves the approved request's audit history with no CANCEL entry. Either choice must be applied consistently to beforeState/afterState (beforeState = the untouched APPROVED row, afterState = the new CANCELLED row).
candidate_options: entityId = original approved request id (beforeState = APPROVED row, afterState = new CANCELLED row)
entityId = new CANCELLED row id (beforeState = APPROVED row, afterState = new CANCELLED row)
write TWO audit records in the same transaction — one per row

open_questions.question: Does the new CANCELLED reversal row participate in balance accounting and in any future aggregation over leave_requests, or is it purely a wire-visible marker?
open_questions.impact: The reversal row copies requestedDays from the original. If any consumer (a future report, a sufficiency check, a balance reconciliation) sums requestedDays over rows with status CANCELLED, the same days are counted twice — once on the approved row and once on the reversal. The balance release itself is unaffected (it is driven by the original row's requestedDays, released exactly once), but the read model now contains two rows for one leave span and nothing in the schema marks which one is authoritative.
candidate_options: reversal row is a marker only — consumers must filter on reversesRequestId IS NULL for any day aggregation
reversal row carries requestedDays = 0 so it can never contribute to a sum
reversal row carries the original requestedDays and consumers must exclude status CANCELLED rows from aggregation

open_questions.question: Should the reversal row copy the original's reason/approvalComment, and should it be linked back to the original in the other direction (a reversedByRequestId on the approved row)?
open_questions.impact: The approved row is immutable, so it can never gain a forward pointer — a client that fetches the approved row alone cannot discover its reversal without querying by reversesRequestId. Copying approvalComment onto the CANCELLED row would also blur the immutability boundary by duplicating approval data onto a row that was never approved.
candidate_options: reversal row copies reason only; approvalComment/approverId/decidedAt stay null; discovery is one-directional via reversesRequestId
reversal row copies reason and approvalComment verbatim
add a nullable reversedByRequestId to the approved row (violates the immutability requirement — rejected unless explicitly sanctioned)

auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: EmployeeRole } where EmployeeRole = 'EMPLOYEE' | 'MANAGER' | 'ADMIN'. Identity and role are obtained from a JWT bearer token verified by the existing registerAuth preHandler (src/shared/auth/index.ts), which populates request.user from payload.sub (id) and payload.role; POST /auth/login is the only public path. RBAC is enforced at the API boundary by resolveActor (throws UnauthorizedError on a missing/invalid actor) and in the service by assertCanCancel — never inline in the route handler. Cancellation authority: the owner may cancel their own DRAFT or SUBMITTED request; only an APPROVED request may be cancelled by a non-owner, and then only by the requester's direct manager (employee.managerId === actor.id) or an ADMIN (exempt from the direct-manager check). All other combinations throw ForbiddenError. The reversal row inherits the original's employeeId, so it is visible under the same role-scoped read rules (EMPLOYEE: own only; MANAGER: own plus direct reports, one level; ADMIN: all).
error_response_contract: Errors return { error: string; code: string } via the routes' sendError helper. Validation failure -> HTTP 400 (ValidationError, code VALIDATION); authentication failure -> 401 (UnauthorizedError, code UNAUTHORIZED); authorization failure -> 403 (ForbiddenError, code FORBIDDEN); not found -> 404 (NotFoundError, code NOT_FOUND); invalid state transition or a blocked cancellation (leave already begun, startDate <= today) -> 409 (ConflictError, code CONFLICT); any other throw -> 500 { error: 'Internal Server Error' }. POST /leaves/:id/cancel returns 200 with the CANCELLED row — for an APPROVED original that is the NEW reversal row, not the original. GET /leaves/:id returns the same 404 for a request the caller may not see as for one that does not exist.
